ABOUT OG GROUP

Built in Cleveland.
Run on itself.

OG OS wasn’t designed in a boardroom — it was built inside a live off-market operation. OG Group runs its own Cleveland acquisition business on the exact screens you’ll walk through in the tours: the same dialer sessions, the same comps discipline, the same deal gates.

The math is non-negotiable. Every valuation starts with sold comps from the same ZIP — a comp from the next ZIP over is not a comp. ARV, the 70% rule, rehab by condition, assignment fee — the system computes the ceiling, and the ceiling is audited.

Around the operation sits the network: an invite-only marketplace where Deal Partners share verified investors and approved deals — because a buyer you share returns to you as everyone’s exits, with your attribution locked.

QUESTIONS

Fair questions.

An operating system for off-market real estate operations: lead pool, power dialer, comps-driven valuations, deal pipeline with stage gates, contracts, title, finance — plus an invite-only investor network layered on top. One login, the whole operation.

It’s a closed, invite-only marketplace. Deal Partners are invited by existing members, and investors join through a partner. Every deal on the board passes a 12-point quality gate before anyone sees it.

Because sharing is what unlocks the board. Share your investors and you see everyone’s — every approved deal from every partner becomes a potential match for your buyers. Don’t share, and the community stays invisible to you. Your investors’ contact details stay protected at the server either way.

You do. Whoever brought the investor owns the split, forever. Attribution is recorded when the investor enters the network, every match is tracked, and corrections are audited — ownership is never quietly reassigned.

Addresses on the board are gated. When an investor wants a deal, they reserve it with a reservation fee — confirming payment wins the deal: contact details are released, the referral reward is created, and the whole action is audited in one click.

No. Each organization runs its own isolated engine. Investor contacts are protected at the server, addresses stay gated until reservation, and even premium share codes — which let a partner bill against your integration keys — never expose a single lead or comp you didn’t explicitly share.
